title: Pre-baked shadow texture vs live box-shadow
variable: baked shadow texture vs live box-shadow
claim: The standard art-pipeline advice - 'bake the shadow into the sprite' - is only worth the asset cost if a live blurred box-shadow actually costs measurably more. This case is the evidence for or against it. Companion case: box-shadow-blur isolates the shadow's cost against no shadow at all.
result: CONFIRMED but small: nothing at 30, then Paint 1.13x at 100 and 1.26x at 300, with RecordRendering 1.18x / 1.30x / 1.25x. Baking the shadow into a texture recovers roughly a quarter of the paint cost at 300 elements - real, but far less than the shadow itself costs against having none (box-shadow-blur measured 2.16x Paint). Read the two together: the shadow is what you pay for, and pre-baking recovers only part of it. Compare gradient-clip-baked, where baking recovered 15x - the answer is emphatically not the same for every effect.
notes: Applicability gate: DIRECT. box-shadow is supported (only the 'inset' keyword is rejected). url() shows as unsupported in the feature inventory, but that entry is a probe SKIP, not a finding - its own evidence says 'treat as present, manual verification recommended', and it was verified manually here: the Player loads both textures with no ResourceRequestJob failure. Rule 1: one variable, how the shadow is produced. Rule 2 EXCEPTION: the tile boxes differ (A is 88x64 carrying the texture, B is 68x44 with a 10px margin). This is intrinsic to the comparison, not sloppiness: CSS paints a box-shadow OUTSIDE the border box, while a texture must reserve margin for it INSIDE. The geometry is chosen so both variants land the same 68x44 rounded rect at the same screen position with the same shadow extent, which is what a fill-rate comparison depends on. Rule 3: identical JS, byte-for-byte. Rule 4 EXCEPTION: A loads shadow-baked.png and B loads nothing - the asset IS the variable. The texture is generated by tools/make-baked-images.js so it is reproducible and reviewable rather than an opaque blob. Rule 5: 300 tiles occupy 1852x1032 inside 1920x1080. Rule 6: shared root-nudge damage driver. Rule 7: no randomness. Rule 8: counts 30/100/300. Rule 9: plain HTML/CSS/JS. Rule 10: expected axis is GPU - a texture blit against a runtime blur pass.
